subject.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic invalid_request_error as format for failover

question: Should status-less structured `invalid_request_error` bodies follow the existing HTTP 400/422 policy and advance configured model fallbacks, including when the rejection is caused by user or configuration input?
rationale: This deliberately broadens provider-routing behavior for existing installations; tests can prove mechanics, but only the shared fallback owner can confirm the intended compatibility policy.

options.title: Align with HTTP 400 semantics
options.body: Preserve schema/replay diagnostics, classify the body as `format` for fallback, and merge after exact-head validation.

options.title: Narrow recognized payloads
options.body: Only fail over known recoverable invalid-request subtypes or providers, leaving other status-less invalid requests terminal.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Do not broaden fallback for status-less invalid requests and close the PR after documenting the policy on the linked issue.

recommendation.title: Align with HTTP 400 semantics
recommendation.body: Preserve schema/replay diagnostics, classify the body as `format` for fallback, and merge after exact-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest sustained ownership of the shared model-fallback implementation and its compatibility semantics.
